n: Jesus offers a sign so people can recognize when God is about to gather scattered Israel and establish Zion again. The sign tells when the latter-day gathering begins.

f.w: I give unto you a sign

n: The sign: when Christ’s words given to these people — essentially the Book of Mormon — are made known to the Gentiles, revealing who Lehi’s descendants are and how the Gentiles scattered them.
These records will come from the Father, through the Gentiles, to the descendants of the people Jesus is addressing. The flow of the message is: Father, Gentiles, then Lehi’s seed.

f.g: From the Gentiles to the descendants of these Nephites and Lamanites.

n: It is the Father’s wisdom that Gentiles be established in this land as a free people, so the record could come forth from them. Many Latter-day Saints see in this the founding of the United States and its religious liberty.

f.w: set up as a free people

n: The record will come from the Gentiles to Lehi’s descendants, who will by then have fallen into unbelief because of sin.
Why through Gentiles? So God can show his power to them too, inviting them to repent, be baptized, learn true doctrine, and be counted among Israel. The gospel is for all.

f.w: the true points of my doctrine

n: When Lehi’s descendants begin to learn these things, it will be a sign that the Father’s work to fulfill his covenant with Israel has already begun.

f.w: the work of the Father hath already commenced

n: In that day kings will be speechless at what they see and hear — Jesus applies Isaiah 52:15 to the coming forth of this latter-day work.
For Christ’s sake the Father will do a great and marvelous work, yet some will refuse to believe it even when a man declares it to them.

f.w: a great and a marvelous work

n: God holds his servant’s life in his hand. Though the servant will be “marred,” God will heal him, showing his wisdom is greater than the devil’s cunning. Latter-day Saints often see Joseph Smith in this servant, especially in the loss of the 116 pages.

f.w: my wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil

n: Whoever rejects Christ’s words, brought forth to the Gentiles by this servant, will be cut off from the covenant people — as Moses foretold.
Jesus repeats Micah’s image: the remnant of Jacob among the Gentiles will be like a young lion among sheep that no one can stop.

f.w: as a lion among the beasts of the forest

n: The remnant’s hand will be raised against its enemies, and those enemies cut off. God’s covenant people will ultimately prevail.

f.w: Their hand shall be lifted up

n: Woe to the Gentiles unless they repent. Now quoting Micah 5:10, God will remove their horses and chariots — the military might they trust in.

f.w: I will cut off thy horses

n: God will also cut off their cities and throw down their fortresses. Human security systems will not save those who refuse God.
He will remove witchcraft and fortune-telling from the land. False sources of spiritual power and guidance will end.

f.g: Fortune-tellers who claimed to foretell the future.

n: Idols — carved and standing images — will be removed, and people will no longer worship things they made with their own hands.
God will uproot their “groves” and destroy their cities. Groves were sites of idol worship in the ancient world.

f.g: Sacred poles or tree shrines associated with idol worship (Hebrew asherim).

n: Lying, deception, envy, strife, priestcraft, and sexual sin will all be done away. Jesus adds this verse to Micah’s list to show the moral cleansing of the last days.

f.g: Preaching for money or praise rather than for God’s glory.

n: The Father declares that whoever will not repent and come to his Beloved Son will be cut off from his people. Belonging to Israel ultimately depends on coming to Christ.
Severe judgment will fall on the unrepentant, as upon those who never knew God.

f.g: Nations that do not know the true God.

n: But if the Gentiles repent, God will establish his church among them, bring them into the covenant, and count them with the remnant of Jacob who inherit this land.

f.w: I will establish my church among them

n: Converted Gentiles will help the remnant of Jacob and gathered Israel build a city called the New Jerusalem.
They will also help gather in God’s scattered people across the land to the New Jerusalem.
Then heaven’s power will come down among them, and Christ himself will be in their midst.

f.w: I also will be in the midst

n: At that time the Father’s work will begin among all the scattered of Israel, including the lost tribes, as the gospel is preached to the remnant of Lehi’s people.

f.w: the tribes which have been lost

n: The Father’s work will prepare a way for all scattered Israel to come to Christ and call on the Father in his name. Gathering is first a gathering to Christ.
The work will reach all nations, preparing the way for God’s people to be gathered to their lands of inheritance.
Quoting Isaiah 52:12, they will not flee in haste, for the Lord goes before them and guards their rear. God’s people will be led and protected.
